skull.description: The bones of the head. They are divided into cranial bones, which enclose the brain, meninges and ear, and facial bones, which form the skeleton of the oral and nasal cavities. Most are joined by immovable sutures.
landmarks: Zygomatic process of the frontal bone
Nasal process of the incisive bone
Basilar part of the occipital bone

species.horse: Long face. The orbit is completely closed by bone (zygomatic process of the frontal bone). Prominent facial crest on the maxilla; large paranasal sinuses.
species.cattle: The frontal bone forms most of the dorsal surface and the poll (intercornual protuberance). Cornual processes in horned breeds, with the frontal sinus extending into them. Complete bony orbit.
species.dog: Shape varies with breed: dolichocephalic, mesaticephalic or brachycephalic. The orbit is incomplete and closed laterally by the orbital ligament. The sagittal crest is often prominent.
species.cat: Short, rounded skull with very large orbits. The orbit is almost complete; the frontal and zygomatic processes nearly meet and are joined by a ligament.

functions: Supports and protects the sense organs (eye and ear)
Forms the passages into the respiratory and digestive systems
Gives attachment to the facial and masticatory muscles

parts.name: Occipital bone
parts.description: Forms the caudal wall of the cranium around the foramen magnum. Its condyles articulate with the atlas, and the nuchal crest gives attachment to the nuchal ligament and neck muscles.

parts.name: Sphenoid bone
parts.description: Forms much of the floor of the cranial cavity. It has a body with wings and pterygoid processes, and carries the optic canal and the openings for nerves to the orbit.

parts.name: Ethmoid bone
parts.description: Lies between the cranial and nasal cavities. Its cribriform plate is perforated by the olfactory nerve fibres, and it carries the ethmoidal conchae.

parts.name: Interparietal bone
parts.description: Small median bone between the two parietal bones and the occipital bone. It fuses with its neighbours early in life.

parts.name: Parietal bone
parts.description: Forms the roof of the caudal part of the cranium. In the horse the two parietal bones meet at the external sagittal crest.

parts.name: Frontal bone
parts.description: Forms the forehead and the roof of the rostral cranium. Its zygomatic process completes the bony orbit, and it contains the frontal sinus and the supraorbital foramen.

parts.name: Temporal bone
parts.description: Forms the lateral wall of the cranium. The squamous part gives the zygomatic process and the mandibular fossa of the temporomandibular joint; the petrous part houses the middle and inner ear.

parts.name: Maxilla
parts.description: The largest facial bone. It carries the upper cheek teeth, the facial crest and the infraorbital foramen, and contains the maxillary sinus.

parts.name: Incisive bone (premaxilla)
parts.description: The most rostral bone of the upper jaw, with a body, a nasal process and a palatine process. It carries the upper incisors, which are absent in ruminants.

parts.name: Palatine bone
parts.description: Forms the caudal part of the hard palate and the borders of the choanae.

parts.name: Pterygoid bone
parts.description: Small thin bone on the lateral wall of the choanae, ending in a hook-like hamulus.

parts.name: Nasal bone
parts.description: Forms the roof of the nasal cavity.

parts.name: Lacrimal bone
parts.description: Forms the rostral wall of the orbit and contains the fossa for the lacrimal sac.

parts.name: Zygomatic bone (malar)
parts.description: Forms the ventral margin of the orbit and the rostral part of the zygomatic arch. In the horse the facial crest continues onto it.

parts.name: Vomer
parts.description: Median bone on the floor of the nasal cavity that supports the nasal septum.

parts.name: Turbinates (nasal conchae)
parts.description: Thin scrolls of bone inside the nasal cavity, covered by mucosa, that warm and humidify inspired air.

parts.name: Mandible
parts.description: The lower jaw and the only movable bone of the skull. It carries the lower teeth and articulates with the temporal bone.

parts.name: Hyoid apparatus
parts.description: Chain of small bones that suspends the tongue and larynx from the temporal bone.

mandible.description: The only movable bone of the skull; it carries the lower teeth. Each half has a horizontal body and a vertical ramus.

species.horse: The two halves fuse early at the symphysis. Very wide ramus. Vascular notch on the ventral border, where the facial artery pulse is taken.
species.cattle: The two halves stay joined by a symphysis that does not fully ossify. There are no upper incisors; the lower incisors meet the dental pad.
species.dog: Fibrous symphysis. Large coronoid process and deep masseteric fossa.
species.cat: Fibrous symphysis. Short, strong body adapted for a powerful bite.

vertebrae_cervical.description: Seven cervical vertebrae in all domestic mammals. The first (atlas) and second (axis) are specialised for movements of the head.

species.horse: 7. Long vertebral bodies give the long neck; spinous processes are low.
species.cattle: 7. Shorter than in the horse.
species.dog: 7. The axis has a long, blade-like spinous process.
species.cat: 7. Similar to the dog; a very flexible neck.

vertebrae_thoracic.description: They articulate with the ribs. In large animals their tall cranial spinous processes form the withers.

species.horse: 18 (sometimes 17–19). Tall spinous processes of the cranial thoracic vertebrae form the withers.
species.dog: 13. The anticlinal vertebra is usually T11.

vertebrae_lumbar.description: Vertebrae of the loin, with long, flat transverse processes.

species.horse: 6 (sometimes 5). The last transverse processes articulate with each other and with the sacrum.
species.cattle: 6. Long, horizontal transverse processes that can be felt in the paralumbar fossa.

sacrum.description: Fused sacral vertebrae. It articulates with the ilium at the sacroiliac joint and transmits the hindlimb's thrust to the spine.

species.horse: 5 fused vertebrae.
species.cattle: 5 fused vertebrae; the spinous processes fuse into a continuous median sacral crest.
species.dog: 3 fused vertebrae.
species.cat: 3 fused vertebrae.

vertebrae_caudal.description: Tail vertebrae. Distally they become simple rods as the processes disappear.

species.horse: About 15–21.
species.cattle: About 18–20. The coccygeal vein on the ventral surface is a common site for blood sampling.
species.dog: About 20–23.
species.cat: About 20–24.

ribs.description: Paired bones forming the lateral walls of the thorax. Sternal ribs reach the sternum directly; asternal ribs join the costal arch.

species.horse: 18 pairs: 8 sternal, 10 asternal.
species.cattle: 13 pairs: 8 sternal, 5 asternal.
species.dog: 13 pairs: 9 sternal, 4 asternal. The last pair is usually floating.
species.cat: 13 pairs: 9 sternal, 4 asternal. The last pair is often floating.

scapula.description: Flat bone of the shoulder. It is attached to the trunk by muscles only (synsarcosis); the clavicle is absent or vestigial in domestic mammals.

species.horse: No acromion; the spine fades out distally and has a tuber at its middle. Large scapular cartilage.
species.cattle: The spine ends in a small acromion. The spine lies nearer the cranial border, so the supraspinous fossa is narrow.
species.dog: Acromion present. The spine divides the bone into two nearly equal fossae.
species.cat: The acromion has a hamate and a suprahamate process. A small vestigial clavicle is present.

humerus.description: Long bone of the arm, between the shoulder and the elbow.

species.horse: An intermediate tubercle divides the intertubercular groove in two. Prominent deltoid tuberosity.
species.cattle: Very large greater tubercle that overhangs the intertubercular groove.
species.dog: A supratrochlear foramen above the trochlea connects the olecranon and radial fossae.
species.cat: A supracondylar foramen on the medial side carries the median nerve and brachial artery. There is no supratrochlear foramen.

radius.description: The main weight-bearing bone of the forearm.

species.horse: Large. The ulna is reduced and fused to it, leaving a single interosseous space.
species.cattle: The ulna is complete and fused to it, with proximal and distal interosseous spaces.
species.dog: Separate from the ulna, which allows limited pronation and supination.
species.cat: Separate from the ulna; it rotates more than in the dog.

ulna.description: Provides the olecranon (point of the elbow), which is the lever for the triceps.

species.horse: Reduced: the proximal part carries the olecranon, and the shaft tapers and fuses with the radius.
species.cattle: Complete shaft, fused with the radius.
species.dog: Complete and separate. Carries the anconeal process (ununited anconeal process is a clinical condition).
species.cat: Complete and separate.

metacarpus.description: Bones between the carpus and the digits. Their number depends on how many digits the species has.

species.horse: Mc III (the cannon bone) carries the weight. Mc II and IV are splint bones. There is no Mc I or V.
species.cattle: Mc III and IV are fused into one cannon bone with a dorsal longitudinal groove. There is a small Mc V.
species.dog: Five metacarpals. Mc I (dewclaw) is small; III and IV are the longest.
species.cat: Five metacarpals; Mc I is small.

os_coxae.description: Formed by the fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis, which meet at the acetabulum. The two hip bones, the sacrum and the first caudal vertebrae form the pelvis.

species.horse: Large tuber coxae (point of the hip). Oval pelvic inlet.
species.cattle: Prominent tuber coxae (hook bones) and a three-pointed ischial tuberosity (pin bones), both used in body condition scoring.
species.dog: The iliac wing is almost vertical (sagittal).
species.cat: Similar to the dog; relatively long, narrow pelvis.

femur.description: The bone of the thigh, between the hip and the stifle.

species.horse: Third trochanter present. Large supracondylar fossa. The medial ridge of the trochlea is much larger and is part of the stay apparatus.
species.cattle: No third trochanter. Large greater trochanter.
species.dog: No third trochanter; slender shaft. Sesamoid bones (fabellae) lie behind the condyles.
species.cat: Straight, slender shaft; no third trochanter.

tibia.description: The main bone of the leg (crus), between the stifle and the hock.

species.horse: The fibula is reduced to a proximal part; its distal end is fused to the tibia as the lateral malleolus.
species.cattle: The fibula is reduced to a proximal process and a separate malleolar bone.
species.dog: The fibula is complete, slender and separate.
species.cat: The fibula is complete and separate.

metatarsus.description: Bones between the tarsus and the digits of the hindlimb.

species.horse: Mt III is the cannon bone and is longer than Mc III. Mt II and IV are splint bones.
species.cattle: Mt III and IV are fused into a cannon bone that is longer than the metacarpal one.
species.dog: Usually four (Mt II–V). Mt I is often absent or vestigial (the hind dewclaw varies).
species.cat: Four main metatarsals; Mt I is vestigial.

teeth.description: Incisors, canines, premolars and molars set in the alveoli of the incisive bone, maxilla and mandible. The dental formula differs markedly between species.
articulations: Alveoli of the incisive bone, maxilla and mandible (gomphosis)

species.horse: Hypsodont teeth that keep erupting through life. Adult dentition 36–44 teeth; canines are usually absent or small in mares, and the first premolar (wolf tooth) is inconstant.
species.cattle: No upper incisors or canines; the lower incisors meet the dental pad. Adult dentition 32 teeth, with the lower canine shaped like an incisor.
species.dog: Brachydont teeth. Adult dentition 42 teeth. The upper fourth premolar and lower first molar are the carnassial teeth.
species.cat: Brachydont teeth. Adult dentition 30 teeth, the fewest of the four species. Carnassials are the upper fourth premolar and lower first molar.

sternum.description: Ventral floor of the thorax, formed by a series of sternebrae joined by cartilage. It carries the costal cartilages of the sternal ribs.
articulations: Costal cartilages of the sternal ribs

species.horse: Usually 7 sternebrae. Laterally compressed cranially, forming a keel with the cariniform cartilage.
species.cattle: 7 sternebrae. Flattened dorsoventrally; the manubrium forms a movable joint with the body.
species.dog: 8 sternebrae, roughly cylindrical.
species.cat: 8 sternebrae, slender and cylindrical.

costal_cartilage.description: Bars of cartilage that continue each rib ventrally. Those of the sternal (true) ribs articulate directly with the sternum; those of the asternal ribs join the cartilage in front to form the costal arch. In dried museum skeletons the cartilage is lost, so in this model it is reconstructed for the sternal ribs to show where they meet the sternum.

species.horse: 8 pairs of sternal ribs out of 18.
species.cattle: 8 pairs of sternal ribs out of 13.
species.sheep: 8 pairs of sternal ribs out of 13.
species.dog: 9 pairs of sternal ribs out of 13.
species.cat: 9 pairs of sternal ribs out of 13.

carpus.description: Two rows of short bones between the radius and ulna and the metacarpus, forming the carpus (the 'knee' of large animals).
articulations: Between the two rows (middle carpal joint)

species.horse: 7–8 bones; the first carpal bone is inconstant. The accessory carpal bone is prominent on the palmar side.
species.cattle: 6 bones; the second and third carpal bones are fused and there is no first carpal bone.
species.dog: 7 bones; the radial and intermediate carpal bones are fused into the intermedioradial carpal bone.
species.cat: 7 bones, arranged as in the dog.

phalanges_fore.description: Bones of the digits: proximal, middle and distal phalanges, with associated sesamoid bones.

species.horse: A single digit (III): pastern bones and the coffin bone (distal phalanx), with paired proximal sesamoids and the navicular bone.
species.cattle: Two weight-bearing digits (III and IV), each with three phalanges; digits II and V form the small dewclaws.
species.dog: Five digits; digit I (dewclaw) has two phalanges, digits II–V have three. The distal phalanx carries the claw.
species.cat: Five digits as in the dog; the distal phalanges carry retractile claws.

phalanges_hind.description: Bones of the digits of the hindlimb, arranged like those of the forelimb.

species.horse: A single digit (III), as in the forelimb.
species.cattle: Two main digits (III and IV) plus dewclaws.
species.dog: Usually four digits (II–V); a hind dewclaw is variable.
species.cat: Four digits with retractile claws.

patella.description: The largest sesamoid bone, in the tendon of the quadriceps femoris. It glides on the femoral trochlea.

species.horse: Three patellar ligaments. The patella can lock over the medial trochlear ridge as part of the stay apparatus.
species.cattle: Three patellar ligaments, as in the horse.
species.dog: A single patellar ligament. Medial patellar luxation is common in small breeds.
species.cat: A single patellar ligament; the patella is broad and flat.

fibula.description: Slender lateral bone of the leg (crus), alongside the tibia.

species.horse: Reduced to a head and a tapering shaft; the distal end is fused to the tibia as the lateral malleolus.
species.cattle: The head fuses with the lateral condyle of the tibia; the distal end is a separate malleolar bone.
species.dog: Complete, slender and separate.
species.cat: Complete and separate.

tarsus.description: Short bones of the hock, between the tibia and the metatarsus. The calcaneal tuber forms the point of the hock.

species.horse: Usually 6 bones; the first and second tarsal bones are fused.
species.cattle: 5 bones; the central and fourth tarsal bones fuse into the centroquartal bone, and the second and third are fused.
species.dog: 7 bones.
species.cat: 7 bones.

atlas.description: First cervical vertebra. It has no body and no spinous process; instead, two lateral masses are joined by dorsal and ventral arches and carry broad wings (alae).

species.horse: Large wings that are easy to palpate behind the skull.
species.cattle: Thick, flat wings; there is no transverse foramen.
species.dog: Broad, flat wings with an alar notch instead of an alar foramen.
species.cat: Similar to the dog, with broad wings.

axis.description: Second cervical vertebra, the longest in the neck. The dens projects cranially into the atlas and forms the pivot for rotating the head.

species.horse: Long body with a spout-shaped dens.
species.cattle: Shorter and more massive than in the horse, with a broad dens.
species.dog: A long, blade-like spinous process overhangs the atlas cranially; the dens is peg-shaped.
species.cat: Similar to the dog.

phalanx_proximal.description: First bone of the digit. It articulates with the metacarpal or metatarsal bone at the fetlock (metacarpophalangeal or metatarsophalangeal) joint and with the middle phalanx at the pastern (proximal interphalangeal) joint.

species.horse: Long pastern bone. Its palmar or plantar surface has a roughened triangular area for the distal sesamoidean ligaments.
species.cattle: Each of the two weight-bearing digits (III and IV) has its own proximal phalanx.
species.dog: Present in every digit; digit I has only a proximal and a distal phalanx.
species.cat: As in the dog.

phalanx_middle.description: Second bone of the digit, between the proximal and distal phalanges.
articulations: Distal phalanx and distal sesamoid bone (coffin joint)

species.horse: Short pastern bone, short and roughly cube-shaped. It articulates distally with the distal phalanx and the navicular bone.
species.cattle: One in each main digit.
species.dog: Absent in digit I.
species.cat: Absent in digit I.

phalanx_distal.description: Last bone of the digit, enclosed in the hoof or claw. In the horse it is the coffin (pedal) bone.

species.horse: Coffin bone, shaped like a small hoof. The deep digital flexor tendon inserts on its flexor surface, and the navicular bone lies behind the coffin joint.
species.cattle: Each main digit's distal phalanx is enclosed in a claw.
species.dog: Carries the claw on its ungual process, framed by an ungual crest.
species.cat: Elastic dorsal ligaments hold the ungual process retracted, which makes the claws retractile.
